items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: this was the Return to Forever with Joe Farrell and Flora Purim and Stanley Clarke

ctx.x: Everything man. I mean look I arrived in New York in the fall of 1971 and in the first six months I was in New York I can tell you who I heard. And you have to remember that I went to clubs as much as I could on my limited college kid’s budget. But there was also a lot of free stuff going on, free meaning no charge. But the first six months I heard Lee Konitz playing with a minimalist named Lamont Young in the Metropolitan Museum actually; then I heard Elvin Jones’ quartet in a little auditorium on the upper west…

with Joe Farrell and Dave Liebman and Gene Perla; I heard the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band at the Village Vanguard, this was the first of a number of times I heard them at the Vanguard; I heard Chick Corea and Return to Forever, their first gig at the Village Vanguard, this was the Return to Forever with Joe Farrell and Flora Purim and Stanley Clarke, and I heard Airto Moreira, this was their first gig ever and it was one of the greatest nights of live music I have ever heard, as good as the records were that they…
Were you ever tempted at that time to call up Mom and Dad and say, “Listen, I’m not going to major anymore in what I’m doing, I have to be a musician.”
